svg.title: How kqueue wakes an event loop
svg.desc: Animated. A thread registers fd 3, fd 4 and fd 5 with kevent(EV_ADD), which attaches a knote to each socket, then parks on the kqueue. A frame arrives: the NIC DMAs it into the rx ring and raises an interrupt, the driver passes it up through ether, ip and tcp, each stripping its header, and tcp appends the payload to fd 5's receive buffer as mbufs. sorwakeup() fires fd 5's knote, which joins the kqueue's active list. kevent() wakes, copies the event out to user space, and read(5) copies the bytes into the thread's buffer.
svg.text: 1 · kevent(EV_ADD) attaches a knote to each socket
2 · kevent() parks the thread on the kqueue
3 · the NIC DMAs the frame into the rx ring
4 · an interrupt hands the frame to the driver
5 · ether, ip and tcp each strip their header
6 · tcp appends the payload to fd 5's buffer
8 · kevent() wakes and copies out the event
9 · read(5) copies the bytes to user space
